subject: Equilibrium ladder construct — marginal vs blended math and waterfall concessions
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Soto <elena@castorhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Oct 2029 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed ladder options for Hosted API commit

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised I pulled together two clean ways we typically structure per-token volume discounts for hosted API commitments: a pure marginal ladder and a blended (slab) ladder. Attached is a short workbook (redwood_equilibrium_ladder_v1.xlsx) showing side-by-side math for your current forecast and a few runway scenarios.

Topline notes:
- Marginal ladder: discounts only apply to tokens within each breakpoint. Easier to reason about at the unit level; tends to be cheaper for the vendor at high growth profiles.
- Blended (slab): a single effective per-token rate for the entire volume tier; simpler invoicing and easier to explain to finance but can be more generous at scale.

We also sketched a hybrid/degression option (bottom tab) that anchors the early breakpoints to a blended floor while transitioning to marginal pricing at high velocity — it reduces your near-term spend while keeping incentives aligned as usage scales.

Open questions for your team:
1) Do you need a predictable effective rate on invoices (blended) or strictly incremental unit economics (marginal)?
2) What percent of your forecast is burst/experimental vs steady-state? We can set breakpoints or a corridor to protect both sides.
3) Any procurement/legal constraints on clawbacks or retroactive true-ups?

If helpful I can share a worked example using the Q1 forecast you mentioned — provides an apples-to-apples comparison for CFO/Procurement review.

Best,
Mina Haddad

Internal note (and looping Rafael + Karthik in):

Elena and procurement are leaning hard to a blended monthly rate for budgeting. Primary asks:
- 90-day lookback window, credits applied prospectively (no retroactive debits).
- Example invoice scenarios for short burst and sustained uplift.

Option A (blended): simplest for client; we can offer a stepped blended ladder with effective per-token rates at each band. Example bands: 0-1B, 1-5B, 5B+.
Option B (marginal): preserves unit economics for us; need stronger runway discounts at higher bands to keep effective price marketable.
Option C (hybrid/degression): create a blended floor for the first ~3 months and transition to marginal beyond a velocity threshold. This buys the customer predictability while protecting our margin at scale.

Attachments: I attached the same workbook and a draft SOW. Mina — attached are two quick, plausible scenarios based on Elena's Q1 forecast (see redwood_equilibrium_ladder_v1.xlsx):

Scenario 1: 2-month burst (spike to 3x steady-state for 60 days)
- Blended ladder: effective rate moves from $0.00042/token to $0.00031/token for the billing month — invoice shows large effective discount that month.
- Marginal ladder: only tokens above the breakpoints get the lower marginal price, so effective blended rate for that month is $0.00036/token.

Scenario 2: 6-month sustained uplift (steady-state increases by 40%)
- Blended ladder: client sees a single lower effective per-token rate immediately after crossing band, which is easiest for finance but more aggressive for us.
- Marginal ladder: vendor realizes less immediate downside; effective blended rate drifts down slower.

Hybrid recommendation (our suggested commercial compromise):
- 90-day lookback window, credits applied prospectively to next invoice.
- First 3-months after onboarding: apply a blended floor equal to the effective rate for the first forecasted tier (protects client budget).
- After crossing a sustained velocity threshold (e.g., >50% above forecast for two consecutive months), switch to marginal pricing for incremental tokens above the threshold.

This structure gives Castor immediate invoice clarity while preserving our ability to capture margin as they scale. I modeled a 12-month P&L column — attached.

Subject: Final proposal: hybrid equilibrium ladder + contract language (90d lookback)

Hi all — following the ask from procurement and the invoice previews Rafael provided, below is the proposal language we recommend for commercial terms. Mina — feel free to copy into the SOW.

Commercial construct (hybrid equilibrium ladder):
- Billing cadence: monthly invoicing, usage reported in token units.
- Effective bands (blended view for invoicing): 0-1B tokens -> $0.00042/token; 1B-5B -> $0.00034/token; >5B -> $0.00027/token.
- Transition mechanics: for the first 90 days after go-live, invoices follow the blended band rates above. After the 90-day onboarding window, incremental usage above a sustained velocity threshold (50% above forecast for two consecutive months) will be billed on a marginal basis for tokens above that threshold.
- Lookback/true-up: 90-day rolling lookback; credits applied prospectively to the next invoice if usage overage is detected. No retroactive debits or clawbacks.
- SLA linkage: SLA credits do not alter the per-token rates; they are applied as separate invoice line-item credits per the SLA schedule.

Contract language (short):
"The Parties agree to a 90-day rolling lookback for usage true-ups. Any credits resulting from the lookback shall be applied to the Customer's subsequent invoice(s) and shall not result in retroactive charges to the Customer. Following the initial 90-day onboarding period, incremental usage exceeding the sustained velocity threshold shall be billed at marginal rates as set forth in the pricing appendix."

Next steps: Mina to send updated SOW & pricing appendix with the attached workbook and Rafael's invoice previews. If procurement/legal are comfortable with the no-clawback + prospective credit flow, we should be able to get to signature within two weeks.

Thanks —
Karthik
